title: The Room on the Mountain: an Engineer, a Foundation, and Fifty-Four Januaries at Davos
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Ravensburg, birth in the machine-works town
stops.date_confidence: attested. Date and place from en.wikipedia, Klaus Schwab, fetched this pass, and corroborated by the WEF's own curriculum vitae as relayed in the dossier. The birth address is not established in any reachable source, so the coordinates mark Ravensburg rather than a building.
stops.campa: Klaus Martin Schwab is born at Ravensburg on the last day of March, in a Swabian town five years under National Socialist rule. No reachable source names the house. His father Eugen Wilhelm Schwab is commercial manager of the local works of Escher Wyss, the Swiss engineering firm; his mother is Erika Epprecht. The papers in the household are Swiss and the address is German, and the boy grows up crossing between the two the way other children cross a street.
suggested_refs: The Escher Wyss works at Ravensburg, managed commercially by Eugen Schwab
sources: WEF curriculum vitae, via the research dossier

stops.name: Ravensburg, the works in the war
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the factory's wartime record, undated as to the year chosen. PolitiFact's fact-check of 8 February 2024, refetched this pass, establishes the Wehrmacht supply, the roughly two hundred forced labourers, the National Socialist Model Company designation, the absence of Nazi Party membership in Eugen Schwab's denazification file, and the committee's acquittal. It does not date these to a single year; 1943 orders the segment. The same check rates false only the claim that Eugen Schwab worked for Hitler, and does not address the further legend that he was a general, ran a camp, or worked on the atomic-bomb programme.
stops.campa: The factory his father manages supplies equipment to the Wehrmacht and employs about two hundred forced labourers drawn from camps nearby. It is designated a National Socialist Model Company. Eugen Schwab's denazification file records no party membership, and the committee acquits him; nothing in it connects him to Hitler, and the later claims that he held a general's rank or ran a camp of his own appear in no document at all. Klaus is five, then six, then seven, a boy in a town whose largest employer is his father's plant.
suggested_refs: The denazification files on Eugen Schwab, cited in the PolitiFact check of 8 February 2024
sources: politifact.com, fact-check of 8 February 2024 on Eugen Schwab, rating False

stops.name: Au, Wadenswil, two years of school on the lake
stops.date_confidence: tradition, not archivally confirmed. The episode is repeated in serious biographical accounts and on both Wikipedias, de.wikipedia specifying the Wadenswil district of Au, but no primary school register has been located and the dossier says so plainly. The year is a placement within the war's last phase, not a documented date. Coordinates corrected this pass to Au, 47.2451 by 8.6434; the figure first carried, 47.2277 by 8.6717, lands about 2.6 km southeast in Wadenswil centre.
stops.campa: The family crosses into Switzerland and settles for a time at Au, a hamlet of Wadenswil on the western shore of Lake Zurich. The boy attends his first two years of primary school there, and the household then returns to Ravensburg. Those two years are where a German-born child would have come by the Swiss ear he keeps for the rest of his life, which is one reason biographers hold on to the episode. The other is that they have nothing else to explain it with. No school register for either year has ever been produced.
suggested_refs: The primary school of Au, Wadenswil, whose register for these years has not been located

stops.name: Lausanne, Mon Repos, the Swiss claim refused
stops.date_confidence: date and citation dossier-sourced, not independently refetched. The judgment is given as BGE 76 I 374 of 21 December 1950 with a link to servat.unibe.ch, which this pass did not fetch. The Federal Supreme Court's seat at Mon Repos in Lausanne is public record and the coordinates are Nominatim's for Avenue du Tribunal-Federal. Schwab was twelve and not in the courtroom; the stop sits at the court because the ruling decides his own status. Note that the research pool filed this coordinate correction under its Geneva listening-device entry by mistake.
stops.campa: Switzerland's Federal Supreme Court, sitting at Mon Repos above Lausanne, rules against the Schwab family's claim to Swiss nationality by descent. What the family requires, the judgment holds, is naturalization, not recognition of a citizenship it already holds. Klaus is twelve and nowhere near the courtroom. Later accounts describe him routinely as Swiss by birth; this is the document that says otherwise, and it is why a question of paperwork keeps surfacing around a man whose whole institution is Swiss. It is dated 21 December 1950 and carries the reference BGE 76 I 374.
suggested_refs: BGE 76 I 374, judgment of the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, 21 December 1950
sources: Swiss Federal Supreme Court, BGE 76 I 374, via servat.unibe.ch, cited in the research dossier and not refetched this pass

stops.name: Ravensburg, the Abitur at the Spohn-Gymnasium
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01-01. Coordinates corrected this pass to Nominatim's figure for Spohn-Gymnasium, Spohnstrasse 22, in Ravensburg's Nordstadt; the figure first carried sat about 600 m southwest in the old town.
stops.campa: He takes the Abitur at the Spohn-Gymnasium in Ravensburg's Nordstadt, a humanistic secondary school where the curriculum runs to Latin and Greek rather than to the machinery down in the valley. Of the school years themselves the record holds a date and a name. The town he leaves is twelve years out of the war and rebuilding on the back of the same works his father managed through it. He goes to Switzerland for engineering, then to Fribourg for economics, then to Massachusetts, and after 1957 he does not live in Germany again.
suggested_refs: The Spohn-Gymnasium, Spohnstrasse 22, Ravensburg

stops.name: ETH Zurich, the Diplom-Ingenieur
stops.date_confidence: year contested and not silently resolved. en.wikipedia says he graduated as a mechanical engineer at the ETH in 1961 with a doctorate in engineering, collapsing two degrees into one sentence and one year. de.wikipedia separates them and dates the Dr. sc. techn. to 1965. The dossier's ETH catalogue citation gives a 1962 Diplom-Ingenieur. This file uses c. 1962 for the Diplom and 1965 for the doctorate, which follows the German encyclopedia and the dossier against the English one. Month and day unknown. Coordinates are the ETH main building, Ramistrasse 101.
stops.campa: At the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology on the Ramistrasse he reads mechanical engineering and takes shop-floor work in industrial firms alongside the coursework, the Swiss arrangement by which an engineer is expected to have handled the metal before he designs it. He graduates Diplom-Ingenieur. The sources disagree about which year and about what came with it, one encyclopedia folding the degree and a doctorate into a single sentence, the other holding them four years apart.
suggested_refs: The ETH Zurich student and graduation registers for the mechanical engineering intake of the late 1950s
sources: ETH catalogue record, via the research dossier

stops.name: Fribourg, Miséricorde, economics beside engineering
stops.date_confidence: the structure is corrected here against the first research pass. de.wikipedia is decisive: he studied business economics at Fribourg to 1963 and was promoted Dr. rer. pol. in 1967. en.wikipedia names a Fribourg doctorate in economics with no year at all, so the 1963 doctorate the first pass carried is unsupported by the source it cited. The 1963 date on this stop is therefore the licence, and the doctorate belongs to 1967. The dissertation on public investment and growth was printed at Ravensburg in 1966 per a WorldCat record cited in the dossier and not refetched. Coordinates corrected to Nominatim's figure for the Miséricorde campus, about 1.1 km north of the figure first carried.
stops.campa: He studies business economics at the University of Fribourg while the engineering degree is still in hand, finishing the licence in 1963 summa cum laude; the doctorate in economic sciences follows four years later, with a dissertation on public investment and growth printed at Ravensburg. Two Swiss universities give him two doctorates, one in technical sciences and one in economics. He will spend the next fifty years putting engineers and economists in the same room, having first put them together in himself. The Fribourg thesis and the Zurich thesis are separate works and are routinely merged in accounts of him.
suggested_refs: The Fribourg dissertation on public investment and economic growth, printed at Ravensburg, 1966
sources: WorldCat record for the Fribourg dissertation, via the research dossier

stops.name: ETH Zurich, the doctorate in technical sciences
stops.date_confidence: year from de.wikipedia, verbatim: promoted at the ETH in 1965 to Doktor der technischen Wissenschaften. Month and day unknown. The thesis subject, long-term export credit in the German machine-building industry, is dossier-sourced from the ETH research collection and was not independently refetched. Same coordinates as the Diplom stop.
stops.campa: He is promoted Doktor der technischen Wissenschaften at the ETH with a thesis on long-term export credit in the German machine-building industry, a subject sitting exactly where an engineer meets a balance sheet. The choice is not abstract. The industry he writes about is his father's industry, and it is the industry that will fill the seats at his first symposium six years from now. This is the first of his two doctorates. The Fribourg one follows in 1967, and neither of them is much quoted.
suggested_refs: The ETH dissertation on long-term export credit in German machine building, distinct from the Fribourg thesis
sources: ETH research collection record, via the research dossier

stops.name: Cambridge, the Kennedy School and Kissinger
stops.date_confidence: attested. de.wikipedia gives the range 1966 to 1967 verbatim; the September start is the academic year's normal opening and is inferred, not documented. en.wikipedia confirms the Master in Public Administration and the meeting with Henry Kissinger. Coordinates corrected to Nominatim's Harvard Kennedy School figure; the coordinate first carried sat about 270 m northwest across Eliot Street. Claims in circulation that the Harvard years involved an intelligence-recruitment relationship are noted in the dossier as unsupported and are carried nowhere in this file.
stops.campa: He crosses to Massachusetts for a Master in Public Administration at the Kennedy School and meets Henry Kissinger there in 1966, three years before Kissinger enters the Nixon White House. The degree is in a discipline that assumes government, business and the academy can be seated at one table, and the American practice of doing it is the model he takes back to Europe with him. Nothing here is doctrine yet. The Kissinger relationship holds for half a century, and Kissinger will come to Davos again and again.
suggested_refs: The Harvard Kennedy School Master in Public Administration cohort of 1966-1967

stops.name: Zurich, the Escher Wyss board
stops.date_confidence: the firm and the merger are attested, the tenure is not. Sulzer's own corporate history confirms the acquisition of Escher Wyss, 53 per cent in 1966 and completed in 1969, and the Zurich seat. Schwab's specific dates on the managing board, given as 1967 to 1970, come from the dossier and were not separately refetched. Month and day unknown. Coordinates mark Escher-Wyss-Platz. The dossier separately carries a study by the historian Peter Hug on Sulzer offers of uranium-enrichment technology to apartheid South Africa in 1977, seven years after Schwab left; that is not carried here and is flagged in the report.
stops.campa: He joins the managing board of Escher Wyss in Zurich as Sulzer absorbs it, and helps run the integration of an engineering group of more than ten thousand employees. It is the same company whose Ravensburg works his father managed through the war, entered now at the top rather than the shop floor. Three years of merger work show him European industry from inside its own management, and show him how little it knows about the American firms outrunning it. He is twenty-nine.
suggested_refs: Sulzer's corporate history of the Escher Wyss acquisition, 1966-1969
sources: research dossier, for the board tenure dates

stops.name: Geneva, the foundation and the book
stops.date_confidence: year attested for both the foundation and the book by en.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted. The foundation's registered address in 1971 is not established in anything reachable, so the pin is central Geneva rather than the Cologny headquarters it occupies later. The book, Moderne Unternehmensfuehrung im Maschinenbau, is listed on en.wikipedia as co-authored.
stops.campa: He registers a non-profit foundation in Geneva to carry the symposium, the European Management Forum, and publishes the same year a book on modern management in machine building arguing that a company's managers answer to more than its shareholders. The argument has no name yet and no manifesto behind it. It is a young engineer-economist's proposition about the sort of firm he has just spent three years helping to merge. Sixteen years on, the foundation will be renamed the World Economic Forum.
suggested_refs: Moderne Unternehmensfuehrung im Maschinenbau, 1971

stops.name: Davos, the first European Management Symposium
stops.date_confidence: attested. Dates of 24 January to 7 February 1971 and the count of 444 participants from 31 countries are cross-confirmed between en.wikipedia and the WEF's own historical account as relayed in the dossier; some renderings give roughly 450. Coordinates are the corpus's canonical Davos Congress Centre pin, inherited byte-identical from yuval_noah_harari.journey.json, which itself corrected a dossier figure about 430 m off. Nominatim independently returns 46.8011 by 9.8308, some 50 m away; the inherited value is kept for consistency across the corpus.
stops.campa: For two weeks in the winter of 1971 he fills a Graubunden ski resort with four hundred and forty-four executives from thirty-one countries, on his own initiative, with nothing behind him but a foundation registered weeks earlier. The premise is narrow: European managers do not know how American corporations are run, and somebody should tell them. He is thirty-two. No head of state attends, no press corps covers it, and nothing on the programme is political. The sessions run from 24 January to 7 February, and then everybody goes home.
suggested_refs: The Davos Congress Centre, Promenade 92a, host of the annual meeting from 1971

stops.name: Sertig Dorfli, the marriage to Hilde Stoll
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia, which also names the Sertig valley church. Month and day unknown; June places the wedding after the symposium and is an ordering device, not a date. The specific chapel is not resolved to building precision and the coordinates mark the hamlet of Sertig Dorfli. Corrected by about 3.9 km this pass: the figure first carried, 46.7595 by 9.863, is not in the Sertig valley at all but up near Clavadel.
stops.campa: Hilde Stoll answered a newspaper advertisement for an assistant in 1970 and spent the year that followed organizing the symposium that has just closed. She will run the organizational side of the Forum for decades, much of it unpaid and untitled, and she will be named alongside him in the investigation that ends his chairmanship fifty-four years later. They marry in a small Reformed church in the Sertig, a side valley climbing south out of Davos to a hamlet of wooden houses and a stream.
suggested_refs: The Reformed church of the Sertig valley above Davos

stops.name: Geneva, the chair in business policy
stops.date_confidence: institution and date range attested by en.wikipedia: professor of Business Policy at the University of Geneva from 1972 to 2003, honorary professor after. Month and day unknown. The specific campus building is not verified; coordinates are Nominatim's for Uni Dufour, about 500 m northwest of the figure first carried.
stops.campa: He is appointed professor of Business Policy at the University of Geneva and holds the chair for thirty-one years, teaching in the city where the foundation is registered and running the foundation out of the same hours. The post is not decoration. It supplies the title he is introduced by and a salary independent of the thing he is building; a professor issuing a manifesto is heard differently from a foundation issuing a press release. He stays until 2003 and is honorary professor after.
suggested_refs: The University of Geneva chair in Business Policy, held 1972-2003

stops.name: Davos, the Davos Manifesto
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia; the exact day within the January 1973 meeting is not given. The quote attached to this stop is not from the 1973 text but from the second Davos Manifesto published under Schwab's byline in December 2019, and the quote_source says so. Canonical Davos coordinates as at the 1971 stop.
stops.campa: The third meeting adopts a code of ethics for management, one page long: the purpose of professional management is to serve clients, shareholders, employees and society, and to balance their differing interests while securing the enterprise's continued existence. It carries no enforcement mechanism and binds nobody. Schwab will spend the next five decades citing this page as the founding doctrine of the thing he built, and in December 2019 he publishes a second manifesto under his own byline, saying it again for the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
stops.quote: The purpose of a company is to engage all its stakeholders in shared and sustained value creation.
stops.quote_source: Davos Manifesto 2020, published under Klaus Schwab's byline as Founder, World Economic Forum, December 2019
suggested_refs: The Davos Manifesto of 1973 and its successor of December 2019

stops.name: Davos, the Chinese delegation
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia states that Deng Xiaoping was invited in 1978 and that a Chinese delegation attended the following year; the dossier corroborates 1979 with less detail. The exact day within the January meeting is not given. Venue assumed to be Davos itself. Canonical Davos coordinates.
stops.campa: Schwab invites Deng Xiaoping to Davos in 1978, at the moment China is deciding what to open and to whom. Deng does not come. A high-level Chinese economic delegation arrives the following year instead, and the relationship that begins at that meeting runs on through four decades of Chinese premiers, ministers and party officials on Swiss mountain stages. Beijing sends its economists to a Swiss foundation at a moment when most Western governments have not worked out how to talk to it. Why the foundation and not the governments, nothing in the record explains.
suggested_refs: The 1978 invitation to Deng Xiaoping and the Chinese delegation of 1979

stops.name: New Delhi, the first India Economic Summit
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The claim comes from en.wikipedia only, is absent from the dossier, and was not cross-checked against a second source this pass. The April date is the dossier-adjacent convention and is not documented; the venue within New Delhi is unspecified, so the coordinates mark the city centre and nothing narrower.
stops.campa: He takes the convening model out of Switzerland for the first time and holds an India Economic Summit in New Delhi with Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, six years before India begins dismantling its licence system. No source records which building in the capital housed it. What travels is the format rather than the mountain: a closed room, a head of government, and a list of executives who would not otherwise get near him. The Forum will run the Delhi meeting almost every year afterwards.
suggested_refs: The India Economic Summit series, from New Delhi 1985

stops.name: Davos, Ozal and Papandreou on one panel
stops.date_confidence: attested, and this stop exists because the first research pass mistook two events for one contradiction. en.wikipedia, verbatim: in 1986 Schwab arranged a first public meeting between Turgut Ozal and Andreas Papandreou, personally inviting both leaders onto the same panel in Davos. The Davos Declaration is a separate event two years later and has its own stop. Day within the January meeting not given.
stops.campa: Schwab personally invites the Turkish and Greek prime ministers to appear on the same Davos panel, and Turgut Ozal and Andreas Papandreou sit together in public for the first time. Two NATO members with troops facing each other over Cyprus, put on chairs at fifteen hundred metres by a Swiss foundation with no standing in either country and no treaty behind it. Nothing is signed. The two prime ministers sit through the panel side by side, and the photographs go out.
suggested_refs: The 1986 Davos panel seating Ozal and Papandreou together for the first time

stops.name: Geneva, the European Management Forum becomes the World Economic Forum
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia, World Economic Forum; month and day unknown. The pin is central Geneva rather than Cologny, since the date of the move to the route de la Capite headquarters is not established in anything reachable.
stops.campa: The foundation changes its name. European becomes World, Management becomes Economic, and the scope written into the charter widens from business practice to international conflict resolution. The renaming follows the practice rather than leading it: heads of state have been coming to Davos for years by the time the letterhead admits what the meeting has turned into. Everything the name will later be accused of, the reach and the presumption, is in the new one. The old one had claimed nothing beyond a continent and a profession.
suggested_refs: The 1987 charter revision renaming the European Management Forum

stops.name: Davos, the Davos Declaration
stops.date_confidence: attested. en.wikipedia describes shuttle diplomacy bringing the two leaders back to Switzerland two years after the 1986 panel, where they negotiated and signed the Davos Declaration with Cyprus near war. Day and month within 1988 not given. Both en.wikipedia and the dossier caution against overstating Schwab's personal role, and this campa credits venue, invitations and shuttling only. Canonical Davos coordinates.
stops.campa: Two years after the panel, with Greece and Turkey close to fighting over Cyprus, Schwab shuttles between the two delegations and brings both prime ministers back to Switzerland, where they negotiate and sign a declaration aimed at normalizing relations. Accounts written since tend to overstate what he did. He supplied a venue and the invitations and went back and forth between the delegations; the decision to sign was taken by two governments that wanted an exit and found the room already booked. The declaration is dated 1988. The disputes it addressed are still open.
suggested_refs: The Davos Declaration signed by Ozal and Papandreou, 1988

stops.name: Davos, Mandela and de Klerk on one stage
stops.date_confidence: the appearance is attested, the arrangement is not. en.wikipedia's World Economic Forum article frames the 1992 meeting as F. W. de Klerk meeting Nelson Mandela at the annual meeting in their first joint public appearance outside South Africa, which is narrower than the claim that it was Mandela's first appearance abroad. Mangosuthu Buthelezi appears in the dossier but not in the text fetched this pass, and has been dropped. The dossier's further claim that Schwab travelled to South Africa beforehand to arrange it is a reconstruction; nelson_mandela.journey.json does not mention Davos at all, which is a gap in that file. Day within the January meeting not given.
stops.campa: F. W. de Klerk and Nelson Mandela appear together at the annual meeting, their first joint public appearance outside South Africa, two years after Mandela walked out of prison and two years before he is elected. Schwab is said to have travelled to South Africa beforehand to arrange it, though Mandela's own record of those years does not mention Davos. The offer is the one Schwab has been making since 1971: a floor in a country belonging to neither party, with the world's press already in the building. What Mandela made of the mountain, he never wrote down.
suggested_refs: The 1992 Davos annual meeting, first joint appearance of de Klerk and Mandela outside South Africa
sources: nelson_mandela.journey.json, which records the release, the Nobel and the inauguration but not Davos

stops.name: Davos, the Davos Pact
stops.date_confidence: attested via en.wikipedia's World Economic Forum article, an independent addition beyond the dossier's coverage. Day within the January meeting not given, and the informal nature of the arrangement means no single documented moment exists to date. Canonical Davos coordinates.
stops.campa: Russian business leaders meeting at Davos in the winter before the presidential election agree among themselves to put their money and their television stations behind Boris Yeltsin, whose approval rating is in single figures. What a handful of private men settle in that room is what a hundred million voters will be shown. The arrangement is remembered as the Davos Pact. Schwab convened the room and did not make the deal. Critics reach for the episode first when they argue that the Forum is not merely a conference.
suggested_refs: The so-called Davos Pact of 1996 and the Russian presidential campaign that followed

stops.name: Cologny, the Schwab Foundation for Social Entrepreneurship
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia; month and day unknown. The foundation's own founding address is not separately verified and the pin is the WEF headquarters at Cologny, inherited byte-identical from larry_fink.journey.json, which reconciled two conflicting research-pool figures to reach it and gives the street address as 91-93 route de la Capite. Nominatim independently returns 46.2252 by 6.1919, about 340 m away; the inherited value is kept for corpus consistency.
stops.campa: He and Hilde found a second institution from the Forum's base above Lake Geneva, this one for social entrepreneurs, people running enterprises whose returns are counted in something other than money. It gives her, after twenty-seven years of organizational work carrying no title, an institution with her name on it beside his. The Schwab Foundation runs its own awards and its own network from the same address above the lake. Its social entrepreneurs go almost entirely unmentioned in accounts of what the Schwabs built.
suggested_refs: The Schwab Foundation for Social Entrepreneurship, Cologny

stops.name: New York, the Waldorf Astoria
stops.date_confidence: the move is attested by en.wikipedia's World Economic Forum article; the venue is not. The Waldorf Astoria is the standard identification for the 2002 meeting but was not independently refetched this pass, so venue-level precision carries real uncertainty. The 31 January date is the meeting's conventional opening and orders the segment rather than documenting a day.
stops.campa: Four months after the towers come down, Schwab moves the annual meeting out of Davos for the first and only time and holds it in Manhattan, as a declared act of solidarity with the city. The gesture reads exactly as intended, and for one week it puts the Forum on a street where anyone at all can reach it. Police lines run for blocks. Anti-globalization demonstrators march up Park Avenue while inside the ballrooms the same executives and ministers keep the same appointments.
suggested_refs: The 2002 Annual Meeting held in New York City rather than Davos

stops.name: Cologny, the Dan David million
stops.date_confidence: the funding is attested, the founding claim is corrected. en.wikipedia's Forum of Young Global Leaders article confirms that Schwab created the group using the million dollars won from the Dan David Prize, but also that the body dates to 1992 as Global Leaders for Tomorrow, was renamed Young Global Leaders in 2003, and selected an inaugural class of 237 in 2005. So 2004 is the prize and the relaunch, not the founding, and the first pass's roughly 100 leaders in their thirties is wrong twice: the criterion is under 38 at selection and the class was 237. dandavidprize.org returned 403 on direct fetch. Month and day unknown.
stops.campa: The Dan David Prize for leadership brings him a million United States dollars, and he puts the whole of it into the leadership community the Forum has been running since 1992 as Global Leaders for Tomorrow, renamed Young Global Leaders the year before. The endowment relaunches it. Every argument that the Forum is recruiting a shadow government cites this programme before it cites anything else. The inaugural class of 2005 numbers two hundred and thirty-seven, every member under thirty-eight at selection.
suggested_refs: The Forum of Young Global Leaders, founded 1992, renamed 2003, endowed 2004, first class 2005
sources: en.wikipedia.org, Forum of Young Global Leaders
dandavidprize.org, 403 on direct fetch, via the research dossier

stops.name: Cologny, the Global Shapers Community
stops.date_confidence: year and founder attested by en.wikipedia; month and day unknown. Canonical Cologny coordinates as above.
stops.campa: He founds a third tier below the Young Global Leaders: a network of city hubs for people in their twenties, run locally, thousands of them, in cities where the Forum has no other presence at all. The pipeline now runs from a hub in a provincial capital to a Davos badge, and Schwab has built every step of it himself across four decades. The critics who describe that pipeline as covert are describing something the hubs advertise. Membership lists are on the website, hub by hub, city by city.
suggested_refs: The Global Shapers Community and its city hubs, from 2011

stops.name: Cologny, the host-state agreement
stops.date_confidence: date attested by en.wikipedia. The dossier additionally cites admin.ch, which returned 403 on direct fetch this pass, so the primary text of the agreement was not read. No signing venue is named in any source consulted, so the pin is the Forum's own address rather than a federal building.
stops.campa: Switzerland grants the Forum recognition as an international body under a host-state agreement, folding a private foundation into the diplomatic furniture of International Geneva alongside the treaty organizations. The Forum does not become one. It remains a Swiss not-for-profit, founded by one man, governed by trustees he selected, with no member states and no accountability to any electorate anywhere. What changes is the standing, not the structure. The agreement is dated 23 January 2015.
suggested_refs: The Swiss host-state agreement of 23 January 2015 recognizing the WEF as an international body
sources: admin.ch, 403 on direct fetch, cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Davos, the Fourth Industrial Revolution
stops.date_confidence: attested. The essay is dated 14 January 2016 on weforum.org, adapted from his 2015 Foreign Affairs piece, and the book follows the same year. Direct fetch of weforum.org returns 403 throughout; the essay text including this quotation was retrieved via the r.jina.ai reader proxy of the same URL, and the same sentence is independently confirmed by en.wikipedia's Fourth Industrial Revolution article citing the same essay. Placed at Davos because the phrase was made the theme of that January's annual meeting. Canonical Davos coordinates.
stops.campa: He publishes an essay and then a book giving a name to the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies, and makes it the theme of the annual meeting that January. The phrase takes. Governments write it into industrial strategy, universities into course titles, consultancies into invoices. Economists go on arguing about whether the thing named is a fourth revolution or a late stage of the third. Nobody settles it, and the phrase is in the strategy documents either way.
stops.quote: We stand on the brink of a technological revolution that will fundamentally alter the way we live, work, and relate to one another.
stops.quote_source: Klaus Schwab, The Fourth Industrial Revolution: what it means, how to respond, World Economic Forum, 14 January 2016
suggested_refs: The Fourth Industrial Revolution, 2016, and the Foreign Affairs essay of 2015 it adapts
sources: weforum.org, essay of 14 January 2016, retrieved via the r.jina.ai reader proxy after a 403 on direct fetch

stops.name: San Francisco, the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution
stops.date_confidence: upgraded from reconstruction to attested this pass. en.wikipedia's World Economic Forum article states verbatim that on 10 October 2016 the WEF announced the opening of its new Center for the Fourth Industrial Revolution in San Francisco, replacing the first pass's vague 2016 to 2017 resting on a weforum.org press page that returns 403. The street address remains unestablished, so the coordinates approximate the Market Street corridor and are not a building.
stops.campa: Nine months after naming it, the Forum announces a centre in San Francisco to do something about it: a standing shop where governments and technology companies are supposed to work out rules for artificial intelligence, autonomous vehicles and gene editing before the products ship. More centres follow in Tokyo, Beijing, Mumbai. The move puts a Geneva foundation permanently inside the city building the technologies it proposes to govern. Which street the first one stood on is not established.
stops.quote: The possibilities of billions of people connected by mobile devices, with unprecedented processing power, storage capacity, and access to knowledge, are unlimited.
stops.quote_source: Klaus Schwab, The Fourth Industrial Revolution: what it means, how to respond, World Economic Forum, 14 January 2016
suggested_refs: The Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution network, from San Francisco 2016

stops.name: Cambridge, the JFK Jr. Forum and the cabinets
stops.date_confidence: the words are attested, the citation had to be rebuilt from scratch and the day is unknown. The first research pass carried this with two anchors that both fail. stops.campa: Back at Harvard half a century after the master's degree, in a public conversation at the Kennedy School, he is asked about the Forum's leadership programmes and answers with the sentence that will follow him for the rest of his working life. He is describing a placement record and it sounds like he is describing an infiltration. The clip is cut, captioned and circulated for the next decade. No correction ever catches it. The words are his and the recording exists.
stops.quote: What we are really proud of now is the young generation... so that we penetrate the cabinets. So yesterday I was at a reception for Prime Minister Trudeau and I would know that half of his cabinet, or even more than half of his cabinet, are Young Global Leaders of the World Economic Forum.

segments.name: The Great Reset and Its Legend

stops.name: Cologny, the Great Reset launched
stops.date_confidence: attested by en.wikipedia's Great Reset article, which confirms a virtual launch rather than an in-person Davos event, with a video message from Charles, then Prince of Wales. The coordinates therefore mark Schwab's own institutional base at the time and not a convening site, since there was none.
stops.campa: Three months into the pandemic he launches an initiative from a virtual forum, with the Prince of Wales speaking by video: the recovery spending about to be released should be steered toward a stakeholder economy, decarbonization and the technologies of the Fourth Industrial Revolution rather than back to what existed in February. He is eighty-two and has been making a version of this argument since 1971. The two words he picks for it are the Great Reset. Within days they are being read as a confession.
stops.quote: A Great Reset is necessary to build a new social contract that honours the dignity of every human being.
stops.quote_source: Klaus Schwab, quoted in The Great Reset: A Unique Twin Summit to Begin 2021, World Economic Forum press release, June 2020

stops.name: Cologny, COVID-19: The Great Reset
stops.date_confidence: date sharpened this pass from a vague July to the day: en.wikipedia's Great Reset article gives COVID-19: The Great Reset as published 9 July 2020 by Forum Publishing and Agentur Schweiz, authored with Thierry Malleret. The quotation attached here is from the June 2020 press release rather than the book, and the quote_source says so.
stops.campa: He publishes the book with the economist Thierry Malleret, five months into the pandemic and four months before any vaccine is authorized, laying out what the initiative means sector by sector. It sells, and it is read by almost nobody who quotes it. The text is a consultancy document in the register of a foundation press release, arguing for green stimulus, better labour protection and public-private coordination. The thing being denounced under its title is a different book entirely, one that nobody wrote.
stops.quote: COVID-19 has accelerated our transition into the age of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. We have to make sure that the new technologies in the digital, biological and physical world remain human-centred and serve society as a whole, providing everyone with fair access.
stops.quote_source: Klaus Schwab, quoted in The Great Reset: A Unique Twin Summit to Begin 2021, World Economic Forum press release, June 2020

stops.name: Cologny, the phrase outruns the initiative
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, single-sourced. Every figure in this campa comes from the Institute for Strategic Dialogue's explainer on the Great Reset, fetched this pass, and none was cross-checked against a second source. The November 2020 date marks the point ISD dates the American broadcast amplification; the process it describes runs from 7 June 2020 to January 2023.
stops.campa: Within four days of the launch a video calling the Great Reset a New World Order power grab passes a hundred thousand views. By the summer an American cable network is calling it socialism. By November the largest talk-radio and cable hosts in the United States are describing it as an elite plan to use the pandemic to seize permanent control. By January 2023 a single social network holds more than two hundred and sixty thousand posts on it and the short-video counts run into the hundreds of millions. The face on all of it is his.

stops.name: Cologny, the sentence he never wrote
stops.date_confidence: the attribution is attested and the date is a placement. en.wikipedia's article on the phrase establishes that it derives from a 2016 WEF-published essay by the Danish MP Ida Auken and a 2018 WEF video, that Schwab neither wrote nor said it, and that his photographs are often used to illustrate it in memes. The stop is dated 2021 because that is when the misattribution to Schwab spread with the Great Reset, not because anything happened that day. The quotation attached is from a different work, Stakeholder Capitalism with Peter Vanham, published 29 January 2021; the pool had misattributed it to a WEF press release, and renderings vary between cannot and can't.
stops.campa: You'll own nothing. And you'll be happy. The line comes from a 2016 essay by a Danish member of parliament imagining a city in 2030, published on the Forum's website, and from a Forum video of 2018 that put it on a card. Schwab did not write it or say it. His photograph is nonetheless the standard illustration of the phrase in the memes that carry it, and he has spent fifty years making himself the face of the institution that published it. Nobody has established when the sentence and the photograph were first put together.
stops.quote: We cannot continue with an economic system driven by selfish values, such as short-term profit maximization, the avoidance of tax and regulation, or the externalizing of environmental harm. Instead, we need a society, economy, and international community that is designed to care for all people and the entire planet.
stops.quote_source: Klaus Schwab and Peter Vanham, Stakeholder Capitalism: A Global Economy that Works for Progress, People and Planet, Wiley, 29 January 2021
suggested_refs: Ida Auken's 2016 essay on the Forum website and the 2018 Forum video that carried the line

stops.name: Davos, introducing Milei
stops.date_confidence: the address is attested, the introduction is a reconstruction, and the two sources disagree by a day. en.wikipedia's Klaus Schwab article carries the 17 January introduction and the new spirit phrase, cross-confirmed with a weforum.org story page that returned 403 on direct fetch. javier_milei.journey.json dates Milei's own address to 18 January 2024 and records the speech and its reception but does not mention Schwab introducing him, so the introduction is not attested within the corpus. stops.campa: Six weeks into his presidency Javier Milei arrives at Davos, and Schwab introduces him as bringing a new spirit to Argentina. Milei then tells the room, which he has elsewhere called the owners of the world, that the West has abandoned freedom for collectivism and that there is no such thing as market failure. The audience applauds. Schwab, at eighty-five, has spent his working life building the stage on which a man is now applauded for saying the stage should not exist.

stops.name: Ravensburg, the father the internet invented
stops.date_confidence: the fact-check is attested and dated, the placement is interpretive. PolitiFact published on 8 February 2024, rating False. The check itself has no location; the stop is pinned at Ravensburg because that is the town the legend is about and the town Schwab actually lived in. The scope limit matters: PolitiFact addresses only the claim that Eugen Schwab worked for Hitler, not the further strands about a general's rank, a concentration camp, or the atomic-bomb programme. The Rothschild-descent claim is dossier-sourced and no independent fetch backs its debunking, so this campa states only that the circulating trees do not match his documented mother.
stops.campa: A fact-check published in February rates false the claim that Eugen Schwab worked for Hitler, and sets out what the denazification files actually hold: no party membership, and an acquittal by the committee. No document in them connects him to Nazi leadership. The same check confirms the Ravensburg plant supplied the Wehrmacht, used around two hundred forced labourers, and held a Model Company designation. The legend that has grown around the son keeps none of these distinctions. It gives him a Rothschild mother as well, on family trees that do not match the name of the woman who bore him.
suggested_refs: The PolitiFact check of 8 February 2024 and the denazification files it cites

stops.campa: The Forum announces that its founder will step back from executive chairman to non-executive chair of the board of trustees by January 2025, with the president Borge Brende taking over the running of the organization. Schwab is eighty-six and has held executive control since 1971. The statement is dated 21 May 2024 and is written throughout in the language of orderly succession planning. Eleven months later he resigns both roles in a single morning.

stops.name: Geneva, the Wall Street Journal report

stops.campa: Six weeks after the transition statement, the Wall Street Journal reports allegations of harassment and workplace misconduct against Schwab by former employees of the Forum. The Forum denies the claims. Wider particulars circulate in the coverage that follows, on the treatment of women and of Black staff and on pregnancy, and the encyclopedic record is narrower than that coverage. stops.campa: He founds the Schwab Academy at Grand-Rue 25 in Geneva's old town, four months after leaving the institution he ran for fifty-four years. It publishes under his own name and continues the argument, extending the Fourth Industrial Revolution thesis into artificial intelligence, longevity and institutional trust. The vehicle is private, small, registered to one address on one old street, and answerable to nobody, which is what the Forum was in January 1971. He is eighty-seven.

stops.campa: Thirteen months out of the Forum he gives a public lecture at the University of Johannesburg's Bunting Road campus, telling an auditorium of students and staff that universities must be rebuilt for an age of machine intelligence. It is the proposition he has been making since the first symposium, that institutions built for one industrial order cannot be run into the next one unaltered, delivered now by a private citizen with an academy and no forum. The university publishes its own account of the evening.
stops.quote: Education can no longer be preparation for life; education must become a continuous condition of life.

stops.campa: A routine security sweep of his private home office in Geneva turns up a covert listening device, apparently installed at some point in the preceding three years. He files a criminal complaint against persons unknown, his second in fourteen months. No public evidence establishes who put it there or what it heard. He built his working life around a room where the important things were said off the record, and on this account he has spent three years being recorded in his own study.
